pattern.pattern_details: This multi-state inpatient Med/Surg pattern is made up of isolated high-cost admissions across several states, not a recurring clinical trend in one market. Sepsis, poisoning, biliary, and hip-fracture-related admissions are the main drivers. The right response is selective case review, not a broad utilization intervention.
pattern.why_it_matters: Rare inpatient outliers can distort trend and may point to one-time severity, coding, or payment issues that need case-level handling.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Route the identified inpatient cases for clinical and payment review, with special attention to the providers and diagnoses driving the largest single-admission increases.
pattern.validation_reason: The pattern is built from one-claim and low-volume admissions across multiple states.
evidence_summary: CO, GA, IN, and OH IP Med/Surg added about $98K total.
A sepsis-related admission at FAIRFIELD MEDICAL CENTER added about $52K.
A poisoning-related admission at WELLSTAR COBB MEDICAL CENTER added about $27K.
The remaining increase came from single-case biliary and hip-fracture admissions.
